title: Delphine Horvilleur, rabbi: 'After October 7, it took me time to speak about the suffering of innocent Palestinians'
subhead: Three years after the October 7 attacks in Israel and the start of the war of annihilation against Gaza, the prominent French rabbi reflects on what these tragedies stirred in her, in the Jewish community, and in society as a whole, as crucial elections approach in both Israel and France.

subhead: Historian Vincent Duclert, co-editor of a recent book debunking far-right falsifications of history, discusses the many distortions of these would-be patriotic parties in an interview with Le Monde.

title: Researcher Paul-Simon Handy: 'Africa succeeded in correcting the map, it must now be able to reshape international institutions and its own place within the global system'
subhead: UN resolutions on the transatlantic slave trade and the world map have brought questions of reparations and Africa's position in the international order back to light. The challenge is to turn these successes into political and economic gains.

title: Bayeux war correspondent awards: Palestinian Mahmoud Abu Hamda photography prize
subhead: The Washington Post, NPR and CNN won the top prizes in the print, radio and television categories for reports from Ukraine, Gaza and the West Bank respectively.

title: In Kyiv, survivors of Chernobyl face Russian bombs: 'Chernobyl was an invisible enemy. War strikes in the open'
subhead: In the Ukrainian capital, the 'Chernobyl House' shelters survivors of the 1986 nuclear disaster, now confronted with Russian bombardments. A drone strike there killed Natalia Khodemchuk, widow of the first victim of Chernobyl. Her neighbors share how their lives have been shaped by these two tragedies.

subhead: The 35-year-old has established himself on Twitch as one of the most-followed political commentators in the US. A socialist, he enjoys the support of the most radical wing of the Democratic Party. But that support is not unanimous, as his comments on Israel and Jews have led to accusations of antisemitism.

title: Trauma endures in Paris suburb after police grenade shatters teenager's jaw
subhead: On September 28, 14-year-old Eden suffered a fractured jaw and lost most of his teeth after he was struck in the face by a tear-gas grenade fired at close range, just a few meters from his high school, where a protest was taking place. Students, teachers and parents spoke of their fear, anger and sense of helplessness.

title: Denmark set to allow return of 'physical force' to maintain order in schools
subhead: Since 1967, teachers could only physically intervene with students if their safety or that of others was at risk. Starting in August 2027, they will be allowed to 'hold a student, keep them in place, or take them to another room' if the student disrupts the class.
